01.actor: Rav Hamnuna, sent by Rav Hisda
01.event: Rav Hamnuna goes to ostracize the Elders of Nezonya for skipping Rav Hisda's lecture, but they say Rav Hisda never answered their question and then pose one Hamnuna cannot answer.
01.turn: Hamnuna cannot answer their question about a castrated slave and they mock his name, calling him Karnuna.
01.outcome: He returns to Rav Hisda, who tells him the question could have been answered from a mishna and baraita.
01.summary: The Elders of Nezonya stayed away from Rav Hisda's lecture, so he sent Rav Hamnuna to ostracize them. They told him they had once asked Hisda a question he never resolved, so Hamnuna invited them to ask him. He could not answer their question about a castrated slave, and they mocked him by calling him Karnuna, a cold fish, instead of Hamnuna. He went back to Rav Hisda, who said the answer was in a known baraita.

02.actor: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva
02.event: Sages returning from Pelandarsin find their boat has sailed out to sea on Shabbat; two walk the whole boat, two stay within four cubits.
02.turn: The sages split in how they behave on the boat.
02.outcome: Gamliel and Elazar ben Azarya walked about, while Yehoshua and Akiva stringently stayed put.
02.summary: A group of sages, including Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva, were traveling by boat when it set sail on Shabbat. Gamliel and Elazar ben Azarya walked the whole boat, while Yehoshua and Akiva did not move beyond four cubits, being stringent with themselves. The passage cites this only as a proof for a legal point.
02.missing: The incident is only cited as evidence in a legal argument, with no real turn or ending.

04.event: Funerals had become so costly that relatives abandoned the dead; Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in plain linen.
04.turn: Gamliel's self-deprecating example broke the custom of opulent burials.
04.outcome: All the people followed him, and today even rough cloth worth a zuz is customary.
04.summary: Burial had become so expensive that relatives sometimes left the dead and fled. Rabban Gamliel then instructed that he be buried in plain linen garments. All the people followed his example, and Rav Pappa notes that even a one-zuz rough cloth is now accepted.

05.event: Rav Anan, whom Elijah regularly taught, unwittingly caused a perversion of justice and Elijah left.
05.turn: Elijah left, returned frightening after Anan fasted, and Anan hid in a box to continue learning.
05.outcome: Anan sat in a box before Elijah until he learned the whole Seder, giving rise to Seder Eliyahu Rabba and Zuta.
05.summary: A man brought Rav Anan a gift and was sent to Rav Nahman, who favored him as a supposed relative, leaving a litigant at a loss and justice perverted. Elijah, who used to teach Rav Anan, left. Anan fasted and prayed and Elijah returned, but now he scared him. Anan hid in a box and sat before him until Elijah taught him the entire Seder.

06.actor: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi and Rabbi Tzadok
06.event: Each rabbi is propositioned by a noblewoman and escapes sin by extraordinary means.
06.turn: Hanina covers himself with boils and later hides in a dangerous bathhouse; Tzadok sits in a hot oven to show the fate of sinners.
06.outcome: Hanina is protected overnight by angelic soldiers; the noblewoman gives up on Tzadok, saying she would not have troubled him had she known.
06.summary: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi. He recited a formula that covered him with boils, she healed him by magic, and he fled to a demon-infested bathhouse where angels guarded him all night. Rabbi Tzadok was similarly propositioned, asked for food, and when she heated non-kosher food he climbed into the oven. He said one who does this falls into the fire of Gehenna, and she relented.

07.actor: The people of Neharde'a and Rav Nahman
07.event: During a drought everyone in Neharde'a sold their mansions to buy wheat.
07.turn: Wheat arrived, so the sales were unnecessary.
07.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled the mansions must be returned to their former owners.
07.summary: During a drought in Neharde'a, everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat. Then wheat arrived, making the sales unnecessary. Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions be returned to their original owners.
07.missing: It is cited as a legal proof, with the story told very briefly.

08.event: Abaye challenges Rav Dimi over Rabbi Yohanan's statement; Dimi falls silent, Abaye offers the answer himself, and Dimi praises him.
08.turn: Dimi is left without an answer until Abaye supplies it.
08.outcome: Dimi tells Abaye he must have been present in the study hall when Rabbi Yohanan taught it.
08.summary: Abaye challenged Rav Dimi with a contradiction in Rabbi Yohanan's rulings. Dimi was silent, unable to answer, so Abaye suggested a distinction based on the verse about Egyptian converts. Dimi replied that Abaye must have been present in the study hall when Yohanan taught it.
08.missing: This is a brief scholarly exchange rather than a full story with an event and a lasting turn.

09.actor: Rav Adda bar Ahava, his host, and Rav Beivai
09.event: Rav Adda's host (a convert's son) and Rav Beivai quarrel over who should hold authority in the city and bring it to Rav Yosef.
09.turn: Rav Yosef says converts cannot hold appointments, but Adda asks about a Jewish mother and Yosef finds the host eligible.
09.outcome: Rav Beivai oversees religious matters and the host the city's affairs; Abaye draws the moral to host someone who can plead one's case.
09.summary: Rav Adda bar Ahava's host and Rav Beivai quarreled over who would manage the city's affairs and came before Rav Yosef. Yosef first said appointments must come from among one's brothers, which excluded converts. Adda asked about someone whose mother is Jewish, and Yosef said he qualified. So Rav Beivai took charge of religious matters and the host of the city's affairs, and Abaye said to host someone like Adda who can plead for you.

10.event: Rabbi Elazar doubts that Shmuel taught a ruling and goes to his lodging to ask him directly.
10.turn: Shmuel confirms the ruling, but Elazar objects from Shmuel's own earlier statement.
10.outcome: Shmuel is silent and gives no answer.
10.summary: Rav Beruna taught a ruling in Shmuel's name, and Rabbi Elazar doubted it. He had Beruna show him Shmuel's lodging and asked Shmuel himself, who confirmed it. Elazar then pointed out that Shmuel had once said that eiruv law follows only the mishna's wording, which implied the opposite. Shmuel was silent.

11.actor: The heirs of a man who willed a palm tree to his daughter
11.event: A man bequeathed a palm tree to his daughter but died owning only two half-shares of palm trees, which the heirs wanted to give her.
11.turn: Rav Ashi asks whether people call two half-trees a palm tree.
11.outcome: Rav Mordekhai reports in Rava's name that people do, so the heirs may give her the two halves.
11.summary: A man told his heirs he was leaving a palm tree to his daughter, but died owning only two half-shares of palm trees. Rav Ashi wondered if that counts as a palm tree. Rav Mordekhai reported in Rava's name that people do call two halves a palm tree, so the heirs may give her those.

13.event: Rabbi Tarfon would bend down so his mother could climb into and out of bed, and boasted of it in the study hall.
13.turn: The sages told him he had not reached even half of the honor due, asking if he would stay unembarrassed if she threw his purse in the sea.
13.outcome: He is rebuked, showing that true honor goes further.
13.summary: Rabbi Tarfon would bend over so his mother could step on him to get in and out of bed. He praised himself in the study hall for this. The sages told him he had not reached half of the honor due her, since he had not yet endured her throwing his purse into the sea without shaming her.

14.actor: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok
14.event: At the wedding of Rabban Gamliel's son, Gamliel stood and served drinks to the sages, and Rabbi Eliezer refused the cup.
14.turn: Eliezer objects that the Nasi should not serve them, and Yehoshua and Tzadok argue that even Abraham and God serve.
14.outcome: They show that even a Nasi may forgo his honor, so the others may accept.
14.summary: At the wedding of Rabban Gamliel's son, Gamliel stood and served drinks to Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok. Eliezer refused the cup but Yehoshua accepted it, and Eliezer protested. Yehoshua said Abraham, the greatest of his generation, served his guests. Tzadok added that God Himself serves everyone, so Gamliel could serve them too.

15.actor: Rav Gamda and the sages Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi
15.event: When Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled against her husband, three sages ruled on her worn clothes and Rav Gamda rebuked them.
15.turn: Rav Gamda accuses them of ruling to favor or against the great Rav Zevid when Rava never resolved the question.
15.outcome: The matter is left unresolved: if she seized the clothes they are not taken, and if not they are not given.
15.summary: Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebelled against her husband while holding a garment. Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi ruled on whether she lost her worn clothes, with Rav Gamda sitting with them. Rav Gamda objected that they were bending the law because Rav Zevid was a great man, since Rava never resolved the question. The conclusion was that whatever she seized stays, and what she did not seize is not given.
15.missing: The two versions of the ruling are told in parallel.

17.event: Peleimu, who mocked Satan daily, was visited on the eve of Yom Kippur by Satan disguised as a pauper.
17.turn: The pauper behaved repulsively and, after being berated, feigned death so Peleimu was accused of murder.
17.outcome: Satan revealed himself and told Peleimu to say, 'May the Merciful One rebuke Satan' rather than mock him.
17.summary: Peleimu used to say daily, An arrow in Satan's eye. On Yom Kippur eve Satan came as a pauper and got himself seated at the table, where he acted revoltingly and spat in a cup. When Peleimu's household berated him, he pretended to die, people cried that Peleimu had killed a man, and Peleimu fled. Satan then revealed himself and told Peleimu to say instead, May the Merciful One rebuke Satan.

18.event: He asks Rabbi Eliezer whose request for water to honor first when both parents ask, and is told to put his father first.
18.turn: He then asks Rabbi Yehoshua what if his mother is divorced.
18.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua says his tear-filled eyelashes show he is a widow's son and sarcastically tells him to give them each water and call them like chickens.
18.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer which parent to serve first if both ask for water, and was told to honor his father. He asked Rabbi Yehoshua the same and got the same answer. When he asked what if his mother were divorced, Yehoshua said it was clear from his eyelashes that he was a widow's son and sarcastically told him to pour them water and squawk at them like chickens.

19.event: Rabbi Abbahu reports in Rabbi Yohanan's name a halakha, and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turn their faces away.
19.turn: Their turning away signals disagreement without contradicting him out of respect.
19.outcome: From this it is concluded that Rabbi Yohanan did not hold that way.
19.summary: Rabbi Abbahu sat and said in Rabbi Yohanan's name that the law follows Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away, silently disagreeing. Another version says Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said it. The Gemara uses this to infer what Rabbi Yohanan held.
19.missing: A brief incident used as legal evidence, without a clear ending of its own.

20.actor: A man who betrothed a woman conditionally, and the Sages
20.event: A man betrothed a woman conditionally and then had intercourse with her.
20.turn: The condition was not clearly fulfilled, so the Sages could not declare the betrothal void.
20.outcome: The Sages forced him to give her a bill of divorce.
20.summary: A man betrothed a woman on condition and then had relations with her. The Sages did not have the authority to free her without a bill of divorce, so they made him give her one.
20.missing: The incident is told in one line with no named people.
